extracted.intended_audience: commercial motor vehicle (CMV) drivers seeking exemptions from FMCSA hearing requirement, FMCSA staff, State Driver Licensing Agencies, industry stakeholders, and public commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) notice describing the legal basis, evaluation criteria, terms, conditions, renewal and revocation criteria, and public-participation procedures for renewing medical exemptions from the FMCSR hearing requirement for interstate CMV drivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority to grant exemptions and publication requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: FMCSA has authority under 49 U.S.C. 31136(e) and 31315(b) to grant exemptions from the FMCSRs. FMCSA must publish a notice of each exemption request in the Federal Register (49 CFR 381.315(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agency must provide the public an opportunity to inspect the information relevant to the application, including the applicant's safety analysis. The Agency must provide an opportunity for public comment. If the exemption is granted, the notice will identify the regulatory provision from which the applicant will be exempt, the effective period, and all terms and conditions of the exemption (49 CFR 381.315(c)(1)). If the exemption is denied, the notice will explain the reason for the denial (49 CFR 381.315(c)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety equivalence standard for granting exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agency determines whether granting the exemption would likely achieve a level of safety equivalent to, or greater than, the level that would be achieved absent such exemption, pursuant to the standard set forth in 49 U.S.C. 31315(b)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To apply this standard FMCSA reviews the application, safety analyses, and public comments submitted. The Agency evaluates whether renewal would likely achieve an equivalent or greater level of safety compared to compliance with the standard (example: concluding renewal for 19 applicants would likely achieve equivalent or greater safety).

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical hearing qualification standard (49 CFR 391.41(b)(11))
rubrics_metrics.description: A person is physically qualified to drive a CMV if that person first perceives a forced whispered voice in the better ear at not less than 5 feet with or without the use of a hearing aid or, if tested by use of an audiometric device, does not have an average hearing loss in the better ear greater than 40 decibels at 500 Hz, 1,000 Hz, and 2,000 Hz with or without a hearing aid when the audiometric device is calibrated to American National Standard Z24.5-1951.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the regulatory baseline from which exemptions are sought; the standard was adopted in 1970 and revised in 1971 to allow qualification while wearing a hearing aid. Exemptions are evaluated against whether safety would be maintained compared to this standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of certified driving records and crash history in eligibility evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: FMCSA reviews each applicant's certified driving record from their State Driver's Licensing Agency (SDLA) to obtain details regarding any moving violations or reported crash data as indicators of future driving performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a driving record revealed a crash, FMCSA requested and reviewed related police reports and other relevant documents, such as citation and conviction information. These factors inform the Agency's prediction of the driver's ability to continue to safely operate a CMV in interstate commerce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public participation and comment-posting procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: DOT solicits comments from the public on exemption requests and posts these comments, including any personal information the commenter provides, to regulations.gov as described in DOT/ALL-14 FDMS. The comments are posted without edit and are searchable by the name of the submitter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To view comments users should go to regulations.gov, insert the docket number, sort results by 'Posted (Newer-Older)', choose the first notice, and click 'Browse Comments.' If the public lacks internet access, they may view the docket at Dockets Operations in Washington, DC during specified hours (call ahead).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice content requirements for granted or denied exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: If granted, the notice will identify the regulatory provision from which the applicant will be exempt, the effective period, and all terms and conditions of the exemption. If the exemption is denied, the notice will explain the reason for the denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This content requirement is mandated by 49 CFR 381.315(c)(1)-(2) and ensures transparency about what regulatory provision is waived, the timeframe, and the specific obligations of the exemption holder; denial notices must state reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms and conditions imposed on exemption holders
rubrics_metrics.description: Exemptions are extended subject to conditions including: (1) reporting to FMCSA any crashes within 7 days; (2) reporting any citations and convictions for disqualifying offenses under 49 CFR parts 383 and 391 within 7 days; (3) submitting annual certified driving records from their SDLA; and (4) prohibition from operating a motorcoach or bus with passengers in interstate commerce. Drivers must also have a copy of the exemption when driving and meet all applicable commercial driver's license testing requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each exemption will be valid for 2 years unless rescinded earlier. The driver must present a copy of the exemption to any duly authorized Federal, State, or local law enforcement official upon request. These specific operational conditions are prerequisites of maintaining the exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal policy and standard duration for medical exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The exemption may be renewed. FMCSA grants medical exemptions from the FMCSRs for a 2-year period to align with the maximum duration of a driver's medical certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewal requires the applicant to satisfy renewal conditions; the Agency applies the same safety-equivalence standard when evaluating renewals. Example renewal effective/expiration dates for named drivers are provided to illustrate 2-year terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for rescission/revocation of exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: An exemption will be rescinded if: (1) the person fails to comply with the terms and conditions of the exemption; (2) the exemption has resulted in a lower level of safety than was maintained before it was granted; or (3) continuation of the exemption would not be consistent with the goals and objectives of Title 49, chapter 313 or section 31136.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FMCSA may rescind an exemption earlier than the 2-year term upon occurrence of these conditions; prior renewal notices and initial exemption notices may contain additional procedural details regarding rescission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preemption while exemption is in effect
rubrics_metrics.description: During the period the exemption is in effect, no State shall enforce any law or regulation that conflicts with this exemption with respect to a person operating under the exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes that federal exemption controls over conflicting State rules for the exempted individual for the exemption's duration.
